cards.context: Side two is the album's slow, watery half; Simon Reynolds heard boredom and bliss as its twin themes.
cards.headline: Ocean music, written with Cluster
cards.snippet: Eno wrote the song with Hans-Joachim Roedelius and Dieter Moebius of the German duo Cluster, who also play on it — the collaboration grew directly out of the sessions that produced their joint album Cluster & Eno earlier in 1977. It sits on the second side of Before and After Science, an album two years in the making, distilled from more than a hundred tracks to ten. Eno called this one 'ocean music' where its predecessor was 'sky music,' and water runs through it: two figures stuck by a river under a falling sky.

cards.context: Kworb's Spotify tally for the song: 22,866,815 streams — near the top of his whole catalogue.
cards.headline: A second life on other people's records
cards.snippet: The song kept resurfacing in other hands. Los Angeles hip-hop group Living Legends built their 2001 track 'Never Fallin'' on a sped-up sample of it, and their listeners traced the sample home — the threads under every upload still record the arrivals. In 2022 a placement in the Netflix series Élite sent another wave the same way. Four decades on, the quiet 1977 recording is one of the most-played songs in Eno's catalogue, with some 23 million streams on Spotify.

cards.context: The stretch listeners quote back most: the opening verse turns up word for word under all three of the song's big uploads.

cards.headline: Like Columbus discovering new music
cards.snippet: I was sitting at an empty beach, listening on headphones when I first heard this album. I will never forget the experience, sitting there, watching the water, listening to something that I thought, had never been listened to before and feeling like Columbus discovering new music.

cards.headline: Samuelsen carries it on strings
cards.snippet: Norwegian violinist Mari Samuelsen performs the song in Christian Badzura's arrangement, with the Konzerthausorchester Berlin under Jonathan Stockhammer, on her Deutsche Grammophon album Mari (2019). One listener: "Brian would be very proud of this!"

cards.headline: The brothers, below the Acropolis
cards.snippet: Brian and Roger Eno performed the song at the Odeon of Herodes Atticus in Athens on 4 August 2021 — a rare live outing for a singer who seldom performs; the recording reached the soundtrack of the 2024 film Eno. One listener: "a precious moment ,in an unsane world, so thankful"

version.versionLabel: Brian Eno & Roger Eno live at the Acropolis, Athens (2021)

film.association: Nanni Moretti's film is built around a family's grief for their son, and the song enters it twice: a record-store clerk plays it for the father, who has come in to buy an album, and it returns over the closing scene at the sea and the end credits. The film won the Palme d'Or at Cannes.
